profile.summary: Emergency management and public health operations professional, about seven years at IEM supporting FEMA, state agencies and local governments: multi-state COVID-19 logistics, tabletop and FEMA full-scale exercises, proposal research, and office operations. M.A., Global Affairs, George Mason University (2016). Former AmeriCorps VISTA with Habitat for Humanity. Lives in Manassas, VA, and follows politics and policy closely.
facts: M.A., Global Affairs, George Mason University (May 2016)
IEM, June 2019 – August 2026: Associate Assistant, Operations Specialist, Project Operations Specialist
EMI Professional Development Series certificate; FEMA IS-100, 120, 700, 800, 2500, 2600
No security clearance listed on the resume

exercises.label: FEMA exercises
exercises.cite: Facilitated full-scale and tabletop exercises for federal, state and private clients (2022–2024), led a Simulation Cell unit at FEMA full-scale exercises two years in a row, and wrote the notes used for after-action reports.

logistics.label: COVID-19 logistics
logistics.cite: Oversaw logistics for COVID-19 mass vaccination and monoclonal antibody sites in Texas, Nevada, Virginia and Florida (2021–2022), and procured and tracked medical supplies across six states.

public_health.label: Public health response
public_health.cite: Supported COVID-19 mass vaccination and monoclonal antibody sites (87,000+ infusions), took minutes at a state public health agency's weekly meetings during the mpox response (2022–23), and attended the APHA and National Healthcare Coalition Preparedness conferences (2022).

rural_health.label: Rural Health Transformation
rural_health.cite: Has tracked how states carry out the Rural Health Transformation Program since November 2025, including which states are on track and which are struggling.

fema_grants.label: FEMA programs & grants
fema_grants.cite: Helped sequence onboarding for FEMA Public Assistance staff by organizing spreadsheets and analyzing the data for decision makers (2019–2020), and helped counties update their COVID-19 emergency grant applications (2020).

intake.label: Disaster intake team lead
intake.cite: Led a five-person intake center for ReBuild NC after Hurricane Matthew (2019), helping homeowners through application questions.

proposals.label: Proposals & contract research
proposals.cite: Found and screened multimillion-dollar opportunities on SAM.gov, GovWin, BidPro and the DHS forecast (2019–2024) and led proposal writing.

project_ops.label: Project operations
project_ops.cite: Operations Specialist and Project Operations Specialist at IEM (2021–2026): assisted project managers on site and helped stand up new mass care sites. His resume summary also names deputy project manager work, not yet tied to a project or dates.

em_planning.label: Emergency management
em_planning.cite: Worked in emergency management and public health at IEM from 2019 to 2026 with FEMA, state agencies, local governments and a large travel company, including emergency forms built on EM best practices (2024).

nims.label: FEMA / EMI training
nims.cite: EMI Professional Development Series certificate and FEMA courses IS-100, IS-120, IS-700, IS-800, IS-2500 and IS-2600.

intergov.label: Federal, state & local clients
intergov.cite: Worked at every level of government (FEMA, state agencies, county governments) and with a major transportation company.

analysis.label: Research & data analysis
analysis.cite: Built Excel pivot-table trackers of multi-state COVID-19 spending, organized FEMA onboarding data for decision makers, and wrote research for a state health agency's trauma training review (2018).

writing.label: Minutes & writing
writing.cite: Kept minutes at weekly meetings (a state health agency during mpox, 2022–23; a large travel company, 2024) and writes proposals and client-focused documents.

office_ops.label: Office operations
office_ops.cite: Handled office manager duties at IEM (2019–2024): office security, first-line IT help, deliveries, conference supplies, Certify expense questions and flights for corporate-level staff, and helped with onboarding and offboarding.

volunteers.label: Volunteer recruiting & interviews
volunteers.cite: Vetted resumes of language volunteers for Department of Defense requests and ran ten scripted interviews at the National Language Service Corps (2018).

claims.label: Claims processing
claims.cite: Processed hundreds of workers' compensation claims a day for California and Virginia at CorVel (2017–2018).

global.label: Global affairs (M.A.)
global.cite: M.A., Global Affairs, George Mason University (2016): globalization and development, global trade, foreign investment, Middle East ethnography, social movements and human rights.

policy.label: Policy & politics
policy.cite: Has tracked states' Rural Health Transformation Program rollout since November 2025, including which states are on track and which are struggling; M.A. in Global Affairs (2016).

community.label: AmeriCorps VISTA
community.cite: Former AmeriCorps VISTA with Habitat for Humanity, working through the lens of building communities.

ics_advanced.label: ICS-200/300/400
ics_advanced.tip: Asks for ICS courses beyond his IS-100. IS-200 is free online at training.fema.gov and takes a few hours, so finish it before applying; ICS-300 and 400 are classroom courses run through VDEM and local emergency offices.

hseep.label: HSEEP
hseep.tip: Names HSEEP. His FEMA exercise work and IS-120 (which introduces HSEEP) fit, so write "HSEEP" into the exercise bullet if those exercises followed it. FEMA's HSEEP course (K0146) is the next step; it needs a sponsoring agency's signature and the State Training Officer's approval.

eoc_tools.label: EOC software / GIS
eoc_tools.tip: Names software that isn't on the resume (WebEOC, GIS or similar). Add any he used on FEMA or COVID-19 projects; otherwise name the systems he has used (GovWin, SAM.gov, Certify).

clearance.label: Security clearance
clearance.tip: Needs a Secret or higher security clearance, and the resume lists none. The agency can sponsor one after an offer, but it adds months; if FEMA contract work gave him a Public Trust or other investigation, add it with the year.

supervision.label: Supervision
supervision.tip: Asks for supervision. Lead with the five-person ReBuild NC intake team and the Simulation Cell unit he led at FEMA exercises, with team sizes, and any staff he trained.

budget.label: Budget
budget.tip: Asks for budget work. Use the pivot-table spending tracking for six-state COVID-19 purchases, and add dollar amounts he managed or tracked if he can.

grant_compliance.label: Grant compliance
grant_compliance.tip: Uses grant-compliance terms (2 CFR 200, NOFOs, subrecipient monitoring) that aren't on his resume. Lead with the county COVID-19 grant applications and FEMA Public Assistance support, and add only terms he worked with.

contracting.label: Federal contracting
contracting.tip: Federal contracting wants pre- and post-award experience and FAC-C or DAWIA training. His proposal and purchasing work was on the contractor side, so aim at the lowest grade offered and show, in his own words, how that work meets each part of the specialized-experience statement.

legislative.label: Politics on paper
legislative.tip: Politics is his strength, but the resume doesn't show it yet. Add a line on following federal and Virginia legislation, any civic volunteering (campaign or party work only for legislative or political offices), and the Rural Health Transformation Program tracking as policy work.

language.label: Second language
language.tip: Asks for a second language. List any language he speaks and the level, or leave it off.

tools.label: Named software
tools.tip: Names software beyond Microsoft Office. Add the ones he has really used; Excel pivot tables, Certify, GovWin and SAM.gov are worth naming already.

cem.label: CEM credential
cem.tip: Values IAEM's Certified Emergency Manager (CEM). With an M.A. and about seven years in emergency management he may meet the experience and education parts already; the training hours, contributions and exam come next (details on iaem.org).

pmp.label: PMP
pmp.tip: Asks for the PMP. It needs 36 months leading projects plus 35 hours of training; the CAPM is the entry-level option if he wants the letters on the resume soon.

flags.gs_edu: GS-7 and GS-9 in most administrative series can be met with related graduate study instead of experience (one year for GS-7, a master's for GS-9). Check the Education section to see whether a Global Affairs M.A. counts, and upload his George Mason transcript.
flags.gs_11_12: GS-11/12 asks for a year of specialized experience at the next lower grade. Answer each part of the posting's specialized-experience sentence with IEM work for FEMA and state clients, in his own words, with dates and hours per week.
flags.gs_13: GS-13 needs a year at GS-12 level: planning or leading work, not supporting it. Apply only if the specialized experience reads like his IEM projects.
flags.gs_14: GS-14 and above usually need years of senior leadership. This is a long shot from his current resume.
flags.gs_low: Below his experience level, but a way into the agency. Use it as a foot in the door if the work appeals.
flags.commissioned: Posted under the Public Health Service Commissioned Corps pay plan. These billets usually go to commissioned officers, not civilians, so read the Who May Apply section before spending time on it.
flags.brief_not_eligible: The brief below found a requirement the resume doesn't meet, such as who may apply, a license or military service. Read its eligibility notes before spending time on it.
flags.status_only: Limited to current or former federal employees or other status groups. Contractor time at IEM doesn't give federal status, so check the hiring paths before spending time on it.
flags.level_federal: Federal resume: two pages at most. Give month/year dates and hours per week for each job, and answer the posting's specialized-experience sentence in his own words; agencies give pasted announcement text no credit.
flags.level_state: Virginia state jobs screen on the application itself: paste the strongest resume bullets into each job's duties and answer every supplemental question in full.
flags.level_local: County and city boards check minimum qualifications first, so put the M.A., FEMA course numbers and years in emergency management where a screener sees them.
flags.level_legislative: Member offices favor ties to their own state, so Virginia roots help most with Virginia members; institutional offices (Sergeant at Arms, Chief Administrative Officer) hire on skills, and DC Council offices look for DC knowledge. Send a short cover note naming the issues he follows.
